paper.title: A SINGLE ARCHITECTURE FOR REPRESENTING INVARIANCE UNDER ANY SPACE GROUP
paper.research_summary: This paper introduces the Crystal Fourier Transformer (CFT), a single neural architecture that adapts its weights to enforce exact invariance to any of the 230 crystallographic space groups. It achieves this by analytically deriving constraints that group operations impose on Fourier coefficients, constructing symmetry-adapted Fourier bases via a dual graph representation, and encoding these constraints into a group-conditional routing matrix (MG) within a Transformer. The model is validated on material property prediction and zero-shot generalization to unseen space groups.

task.task_name_raw: developing a single machine learning architecture that is capable of adapting its weights automatically to enforce invariance to any input space group
task.objective: To develop a single, adaptive neural architecture that enforces exact invariance to any crystallographic space group by leveraging symmetry-adapted Fourier bases and group-conditional routing.
target_properties: zero-shot generalization to unseen space groups
constraints: exact invariance to any of the 230 space groups
parameter sharing across all space groups
overcoming data sparsity for rare groups
output_goal: material property predictions (e.g., total energy, band gap)
zero-shot predictions for unseen space groups

evidence.text: In this work we present a new approach to crystallographic symmetries by developing a single machine learning architecture that is capable of adapting its weights automatically to enforce invariance to any input space group.

stages.stage_name_raw: using data from the Materials Project
stages.stage_goal: Acquire crystal structure data and material property labels for training and evaluation.
stage_output: dataset of crystals with known properties

evidence.text: For our primary benchmark experiments, we use data from the Materials Project, one of the largest databases of computational material properties (Jain et al., 2013). The task is to predict four key material properties from the crystal structure: total energy (eV/atom), band gap (eV), bulk modulus (log GPa), and shear modulus (log GPa). For each material, the model receives the atomic numbers and fractional coordinates of atoms within the unit cell, the 3×3 lattice vectors, and the corresponding space group identifier (1-230). At the time of training, there were 152,149 crystals with known total energies and band gaps, and 11,997 crystals with known bulk and shear moduli in the Materials Project database.

stages.stage_name_raw: constructing synthetic dataset for orbit distance validation
stages.stage_goal: Generate synthetic crystal pairs with ground-truth orbit distances to pretrain and validate the symmetry-adapted encoding module.
stage_output: synthetic dataset of 100,000 samples per space group

evidence.text: We construct a synthetic dataset containing 100,000 samples for each of the 230 space groups. Each sample consists of a pair of random atomic positions as fractional coordinates in [0, 1)3, a space group, and randomly generated lattice vectors that satisfy the constraints of the Bravais lattice for the group.

stages.stage_name_raw: computing orbit distance as ground truth
stages.stage_goal: Calculate the orbit distance dG(x1, x2) = minϕ1,ϕ2∈G ||ϕ1(x1) − ϕ2(x2)||2 for each pair of atomic positions in the synthetic dataset.

evidence.text:
The orbit distance is defined as
dG(x1, x2) := minϕ1,ϕ2∈G ||ϕ1(x1) −ϕ2(x2)||2.
(8)
It measures the shortest Euclidean distance between any two points in the respective orbits of the atoms, which stays invariant to applications of group actions to either atom.

stages.stage_name_raw: pretraining the symmetry-adapted positional encoding module
stages.stage_goal: Train the G-invariant encoding module to produce embeddings where Euclidean distance matches the ground-truth orbit distance.

evidence.text: The model is trained to minimize the Mean Squared Error (MSE) between the L2 distance of the output embeddings and the ground-truth orbit distance.

stages.stage_name_raw: training the full CFT architecture for material property prediction
stages.stage_goal: Train the complete Crystal Fourier Transformer using pre-trained positional encodings to predict material properties.
stage_output: fully trained CFT model for material property prediction

evidence.text: We use the pre-trained positional encoding model from Section 5.2 to initialize the positional encodings in CFT. This initialization captures the physical scale of the crystal in this feature space, which is important because the Fourier-based encoding is dimensionless. The positional encoding is directly added to a learned embedding for the atom’s chemical element, which forms the input tokens to a standard Transformer encoder with three multi-head self-attention layers with eight heads each, followed by mean pooling and a MLP that outputs the final prediction.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluating CFT on material property prediction benchmarks
stages.stage_goal: Assess the performance of the trained CFT against state-of-the-art baselines on standard material property prediction tasks.
stage_output: test MAE for total energy, band gap, bulk modulus, shear modulus

evidence.text: Table 1 shows the test MAE for CFT and baseline models. Our CFT model achieves competitive performance across all four properties and outperforms all baselines on Total Energy and Shear Moduli prediction. Notably, it significantly surpasses the Transformer baseline that uses standard positional encodings, demonstrating the usefulness of the symmetry-adapted encoding.

stages.stage_name_raw: holding out inversion-symmetric space groups for zero-shot evaluation
stages.stage_goal: Select a subset of space groups (those with inversion symmetry) to serve as unseen groups for zero-shot generalization testing.
stage_output: held-out set Ginv of centrosymmetric space groups

evidence.text: We test this hypothesis in a zero-shot setting by holding out all space groups containing inversion symmetry from the training set.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluating zero-shot generalization to unseen space groups
stages.stage_goal: Measure the performance degradation of CFT when predicting properties for materials from space groups it was never trained on.
stage_input: CFT model trained only on non-centrosymmetric groups
test set of materials from Ginv
stage_output: group-wise MAE gaps (∆MAEG) and group-balanced absolute performance gap (GB-Gap)

evidence.text:
For each held-out inversion group G ∈Ginv, we compute the group-wise MAE under the zero-shot and all-data training regimes, denoted MAEzero-shot_G and MAEall-data_G. We define the performance gap for group G as
∆MAEG = MAEzero-shot_G −MAEall-data_G.
